description: Element Reliability Dashboard — shows the stability and success rates of UI elements across automated interactions, helping users identify flaky elements that may cause automation failures.

groups.name: Reliability Overview Statistics
groups.description: Users need summary statistics showing how many elements are stable vs flaky vs unreliable, providing a quick assessment of automation health across all tracked elements.

assertions.description: Users can identify the Element Reliability dashboard and understand its purpose as a tool for evaluating UI element stability across automated interactions
Users can see the count of stable elements (>=95% success rate), giving them confidence in the proportion of elements that reliably work during automation
Users can see the count of flaky elements (>=80% but <95% success rate), identifying elements that intermittently fail and may need selector improvements
Users can see the count of unreliable elements (<80% success rate), highlighting the most problematic elements that need immediate attention

groups.name: Elements by Reliability
groups.description: Users need to see individual elements sorted by reliability, with success rates and interaction counts, to identify which specific elements need attention or alternative selectors.

assertions.description: Users can see a section listing individual elements sorted by their reliability scores, enabling targeted investigation of problematic elements
Each element row displays its success rate as a percentage so users can quickly assess how reliably each element is found and interacted with
Each element row shows the total number of interactions, providing context for whether the reliability percentage is based on a statistically meaningful sample size

groups.name: Loading, Error, and Empty States
groups.description: Users need clear feedback during loading, error, and empty states so they understand the system status.

assertions.description: Users see a loading indicator while element reliability data is being fetched, preventing confusion about a blank screen
Users see a clear error message when element data fails to load, helping them understand that a technical issue occurred rather than there being no data
Users see a clear empty state message when no element data exists yet, indicating that this is expected for new setups
Users see guidance text explaining how to populate element reliability data by running automations, reducing confusion about next steps

criteria.textContent: Run some automations to build up element history

groups.name: Reliability Color-Coded Badges
groups.description: Reliability badges use color coding to quickly communicate element health: green for stable (>=95%), yellow for flaky (>=80%), red for unreliable (<80%).

assertions.description: Stable elements display a green badge indicating high reliability (>=95% success rate), providing immediate positive visual feedback
Flaky elements display a yellow badge indicating moderate reliability (>=80% but <95%), signaling caution without alarm
Unreliable elements display a red badge indicating low reliability (<80%), drawing immediate attention to elements that need remediation

groups.name: Element Data Rendering
groups.description: Each element row must render its element ID, total interaction count, and success rate percentage accurately from the API data. The summary cards must show correct counts of stable (>=95%), flaky (>=80%), and unreliable (<80%) elements computed from the success_rate field.

assertions.description: Each element row displays a success rate as a whole percentage (e.g. '94%') computed from the element's success_rate field (0-1 float multiplied by 100 and rounded)
Each element row shows the total number of interactions (e.g. '47 interactions') providing volume context for the reliability assessment
Each element row displays the element_id as a monospace identifier, or 'Unknown' when the element_id is empty

groups.name: Required UI Elements
groups.description: All structural elements must be present for the dashboard to function: the Shield header icon, the 3-column summary grid, the scrollable element list container, and reliability badge components.

assertions.description: The Shield icon is present in the header alongside the 'Element Reliability' title
The 3-column summary grid showing Stable, Flaky, and Unreliable counts is present above the element list

groups.name: State Transitions
groups.description: The dashboard transitions cleanly between loading, error, empty, and data states. Summary card counts must be mathematically consistent with the element list (stable + flaky + unreliable = total elements).

assertions.description: When data loads, the 'Loading element data...' message is replaced by the summary cards and element list — both never shown simultaneously
assertions.precondition: Page has just loaded and is fetching from /ui-bridge/history/flaky

assertions.description: The sum of Stable + Flaky + Unreliable counts in the summary cards equals the total number of element rows in the list below
assertions.precondition: Data has loaded successfully (not in loading/error/empty state)

metadata.author: Joshua Spinak
preconditions: Requires UI Bridge automation runs to have occurred — element interaction history is populated during workflow execution with UI Bridge-connected apps
Empty state is valid on fresh installs
backendDependencies: GET /ui-bridge/history/flaky — returns ElementReliability[] with element_id, success_rate (0-1 float), total_interactions
